content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"List the available project documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any documents describing radiator aging/lifetime requirements or operational constraints. Extract the three allowed radiator candidates, their relevant properties, and any lifetime/performance stability limits."},{"id":"s2","description":"From the document review, eliminate any candidate radiator that does not satisfy the lifetime/performance stability constraint or other stated project constraints. Identify the remaining viable candidates to simulate over the allowed 1–6 cm thickness range."},{"id":"s3","description":"Run simulate_separation for each viable radiator at integer thicknesses from 1 cm through 6 cm. Record the pion/kaon separation values numerically for later comparison."},{"id":"s4","description":"If the best result from the integer scan is not at a boundary, run additional simulations near the best thickness with finer spacing as allowed by the simulator, focusing on the local maximum for that radiator and any close competitors."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare all simulated separation results while enforcing the constraints from the documents. Select the radiator and thickness that gives the highest valid pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c, and prepare the recommended choice for final reporting."}]}
